title: Gusto Pricing 2026 for 5, 15, and 50 Employees
summary: Gusto pricing charges a flat monthly base fee plus per-employee costs on some plans. See all tiers and their total costs to find your best payroll fit.
body_markdown:
## Hidden Gusto costs and limits buyers hit


**Five charges sit outside the headline per-person rate** , and each one moves the monthly bill at a different headcount, so price them before you sign.


Gusto bills contractors per contractor, so a team that leans on freelancers pays more than its employee count suggests. **Extra-state filing costs $85 per state per month** , so a team with employees in three additional states adds $255 a month.


Because Gusto charges benefits and add-ons per person, they grow with every hire. Gusto may bundle year-end filings or bill them separately depending on plan, which can put a lump on your December invoice.


[Support](https://support.gusto.com/article/222579327100000/) tiers and plan-gated features decide whether you pay for an upgrade just to get a tool you assumed was included.


### Contractors and multi-state payroll


At $85 a month, the state fee is a recurring cost, which is $1,020 per state per year.


Bought separately, registration is a one-time purchase, and[Fiscorra](https://fiscorra.com/usa/state-tax-id-registration/) lists ReVerify at $150 per state, Regcrest at $180, Middesk at $199 and Aureus Advisory at $499.

Buying registration separately is a one-time cost while Gusto's add-on recurs, so compare the totals before choosing. Count your contractors too, since each one is a line item.


Ask for the all-in figure at your exact headcount. Benefits administration and similar add-ons are quoted per person, and a small per-person fee multiplied by thirty people is a different number than the one on the pricing page.


A tool you need may be available only on higher tiers. Before comparing prices, list the features you need and check which plan holds each one. The cheapest plan that lacks a needed feature isn't the cheapest option.


### Gusto support and onboarding limits


When a deposit goes wrong, thin support matters most. The IRS charges 2% of the unpaid deposit when it's 1-5 days late, 5% at 6-15 days, and 10% at 16 or more days.


After an IRS notice the rate rises to 15%.


On a $10,000 deposit, that means $200 for a short delay and $1,500 once a notice arrives. One setup error that goes unresolved for two weeks can cost more than a year of upgraded support, so weigh the support tier against that risk.
